text:
Lena: quick morning sync - overnight bring-up for heron-liteq-int6 (ptq variant) against the toolcall/structured harness. Overall quality looks ok but we have ~2.3% parse failures. Pattern differs from usual trailing-comma stuff: lots of missing closing bracket or NDJSON-like dumps (model emits multiple JSONs separated by newlines).

Oscar: ugh. can you paste a raw capture?

Lena: pasted one from the harness:```
Output:
{
  \"tool\": \"search\",
  \"args\": [\"redwood inference\"]

{\"tool\":\"click\",\"args\": [\"result-3\"]}
``` So we got two objects, no array wrapper, plus a blank line in between. Our parser expects a single object matching the action schema so it fails.

Priya: OK. Two immediate quick fixes: 1) greedy-extractor that finds the first balanced JSON object in the stream and ignores extraneous NDJSON afterwards; 2) NDJSON-accept mode: if multiple top-level objects are present, treat as a list and pick first matching schema entry. Both are sanitizer-layer approaches.

Oscar: prefer extractor-first (cheap) but we need guardrails. If extractor pulls partial object that misses fields we might mistakenly accept a broken action. Add a check: only accept extracted JSON when required keys are present and types match.

Lena: agreed. Plan: run 3-branch AB test on 15k calls: A = baseline (no sanitizer), B = extractor + schema check, C = extractor + schema check + immediate retry (temp=0.0, max_new_tokens=64, instruct: "return only valid JSON, nothing else"). Track parse success, semantic match (tool + args vs golden), false-accept (extractor accepted but missing fields), latency p50/p95, extra-token cost.

Priya: also add a decoder-tweak branch where we apply logit-scaling factor 0.9 on punctuation tokens for the canary (hoping to reduce stray braces/noise). Might reduce recall on some intents but worth measuring.

qa-bot: kicked off job: "heron-int6-structured-abtest-15k" - ETA ~35m :gear:

deploy-bot: run queued: id=run-20260323-07-heron-int6-abtest :white_check_mark:

Oscar: one more axis - long-context vs fresh prompt. Add a sub-split: (1) last-turn-only prompt, (2) full 4-turn context. I've seen more NDJSON in multi-turn.

Lena: good call. We'll also collect examples where extractor clipped content so we can do manual triage. Priya - can you hook sampling to the triage dashboard?

Priya: yup - I'll add a sampling rule: log up to 200 clipped examples per run, annotate with kvcache length and token budget.

Lena: timeline: results summary + sample dump + proposed sanitizer PR by EOD tomorrow. If B or C drops parse failures below 0.4% with <0.2% false-accepts and negligible latency hit, we can ship as a runtime fallback.

Oscar: add note to include cost delta (tokens per call) so product eval can weigh cost vs benefit.

Lena: will do. Thanks all :sparkles:
